sample_record.CAUSE: Blockage Fats Oil Grease,Blockage Rags wipes,

cadence: Each business day; spills appear within about one day of start (three rows dated 2026-11-02 on the 2026-11-03 file). Law: immediate notice to EPD.
history: Rolling 30 days only. Older daily files are at the same URL pattern (not tested); WWALS has archived daily copies as HTML since Dec 2018.
status_reason: Statewide rolling 30-day list of municipal sewage spills, updated each business day, as an Excel file whose URL carries the date. Day precision, permit number, location address, gallons, river basin, waterway impacted. First feed (with daily snapshots to build history).
notes: "A zero in the quantity field indicates the amount of the spill has not been determined." Quantity blank at first for many rows. No row id: key on permit + begin date + location.

name: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-3-6-.05 Emergency Actions (spills and major spills by POTWs)
operator: Georgia Board of Natural Resources / EPD
status_reason: Public-notice duties: media within 24 hours, sign at the site immediately for at least 7 days, legal organ within 7 days for a major spill, downstream water suppliers within 24 hours.
notes: (2) "spill" = "any discharge of raw sewage by a Publicly Owned Treatment Works (POTW) to the waters of the State"; major spill = "in excess of 10,000 gallons" or causing water-quality violations. (3)(a) "shall immediately notify the Division, in person or by telephone, when a spill or a major spill occurs"; written report in 5 days. (3)(e) report to television, radio and print media within 24 hours. (3)(g) "shall immediately post a notice as close as possible to where the spill or major spill occurred", for at least seven days after it ceases. (3)(b) legal organ notice within 7 days for a major spill. (3)(c) monitoring for at least one year after a major spill. Quotes from the Cornell LII rendering (raw/rule-391-3-6-05.html); (3)(f) also requires immediate report to the local health department; (3)(g) signs also "along the portions of the waterway affected by the incident (i.e. at bridge crossings, trails, boat ramps, recreational areas, and other points of public access ...)".
